problem: Monolithic multi-modal navigation policies struggle to align heterogeneous, noisy modalities and need large models. Existing multi-agent navigation mostly uses homogeneous agents with the same sensors, so cross-modal collaboration among modality-specialized agents is underexplored.
motivation: High-quality, aligned multi-modal data is hard to obtain, and rich-modal models are large and costly to deploy. Splitting modalities across lightweight agents that collaborate without communication could be more scalable and robust. It is unclear which modalities and team configurations help.
key_idea: Assign complementary modalities (audio, vision) to separate decentralized agents trained with CTDE MARL (PPO), using auxiliary target location/category beliefs from audio and a centralized critic that sees the global state.
insight: Heterogeneous audio+vision agents beat a monolithic full-modal agent when targets have clean modality-specific cues (Ranch 64.62 vs AVLA-Collab 18.93). The full-modal baseline is capacity-limited: with embedding size 180 it reaches 73.33 versus CRONA's 68.75, while CRONA stays stable across sizes. The ablations show that the location belief and the critic's state input are the most critical components: without state, success falls below 0.2%, and without location belief it falls roughly by half.
method: Auxiliary belief predictor: for audio agents, a ResNet-style CNN on the binaural spectrogram predicts the sound-source goal (2D, converted to a relative location via pose rotation) and a multi-label category belief. Both are EMA-smoothed (α=0.5) and trained with MSE plus BCE supervised by the nearest target's location and the target categories.

Modality-specific encoders: a ResNet-18-style encoder for 16x16 depth, a 3-layer CNN for audio, and a MiniLM language encoder for the goal text. Their outputs are concatenated with pose to form the observation embedding.

Attention history encoder: a cache of the past k=150 observation embeddings and actions is processed by a 1-layer, 8-head transformer encoder-decoder to produce the history embedding, giving each agent a policy π(a|h,b).

Centralized multi-modal critic: during training only, V(joint history embeddings, beliefs, global state) is trained with a clipped value loss. The global state includes target locations, agent poses and completion flags. An appendix proposition argues this is unbiased under an accurate belief.

Shared PPO-style optimization: encoders, belief predictor and transformer are shared between actors and critic, with separate heads. Actors use a clipped surrogate with a shared GAE advantage and entropy bonus. The shared trunk uses a loss weighted by μ=0.67.

Benchmark: two agents in 5 Matterport3D scenes (Studio, Corridor, Apartment, Ranch, Maze) with SoundSpaces-style audio. Vision is restricted to 16x16 depth with a 10° HFoV and 5 m range. There is no inter-agent communication and the reward is a shared team reward.

setting.backbone: Lightweight per-agent ResNet-18-style depth encoder, 3-layer audio CNN, MiniLM language encoder and a 1-layer transformer, trained from scratch with MAPPO-style PPO (CTDE)
setting.model_size: about 28 MiB total (embedding size 100); AVLA-Collab about 38 MiB
setting.training_data: Self-collected episodes in 5 Matterport3D scenes, roughly 218-252 training episodes per scene (3:1 train/val split), based on SoundSpaces base episodes, trained online with RL for 8000 updates
setting.observation: Per-agent egocentric 16x16 depth (vision agent) or binaural spectrogram (audio agent), plus pose and a natural-language goal; no communication
setting.action_space: Low-level discrete navigation actions including stop (2D navigable grid)
setting.simulator: Habitat with Matterport3D and SoundSpaces-style audio (librosa)
setting.privileged: Global state (target locations, agent poses, completion flags) and GT target locations for belief supervision are used only in training; none at test time

numbers_note: Custom benchmark of 5 Matterport3D scenes, not a standard one. The 'val' split is inferred from the 3:1 train/val split. 'Detect' values are printed as-is (e.g. 1.69) and their units are unclear despite the caption saying %. Aggregate success is given only in a figure.
results: On the custom 2-agent audio-visual benchmark, CRONA is best on Studio (95.72) and Ranch (64.62, vs 42.15 for ALA-Collab and 18.93 for AVLA-Collab) and has the best aggregate success. It is second on Apartment (68.52 vs 78.96 for VLA-Collab). It is weaker on Corridor (21.50 vs 25.31) and Maze (12.13 vs 26.16 for AVLA-Collab). All collaborative methods far exceed the single-agent baseline, e.g. 0.00 success on Maze.
limitations: Only vision (restricted 16x16 depth) and audio are studied, and the tasks are 2D navigation in 5 hand-picked scenes with 2 agents and roughly 200 training episodes each.
CRONA does not win in every scene (Corridor, Maze, Apartment), and only location and category beliefs are explored.
Evaluation relies on training-time curves averaged over 5 runs with no separate held-out test set.
builds_on: Centralized critics with state (Lyu et al. 2023)
